words.enDefinition: a bond backed by specified assets that can support the holders' claims if the issuer defaults

examples.en: The term sheet described a secured bond backed by equipment owned by the fictional issuer.
examples.zh: 条款概要介绍了一只「有担保物的债券」，担保物是虚构发行人所有的设备。

examples.en: Our lecturer asked which assets supported the secured bond in the second example on the worksheet.
examples.zh: 讲师问，练习表第二例里的「有担保物的债券」由哪些资产提供担保。

words.enDefinition: a bond that relies on the issuer's promise to pay without a claim on specified pledged assets

examples.en: The class compared the unsecured bond with a note backed by specific machinery in the case.
examples.zh: 课堂把「无担保物债券」与案例中由指定机器担保的一只票据作了比较。

examples.en: The unsecured bond had a guarantor, but its terms did not pledge any specific assets.
examples.zh: 这只「无担保物债券」有保证人，但条款未设定任何特定资产作为担保。

words.enDefinition: a bond that ranks as senior debt and is backed by assets pledged as collateral

examples.en: The sample issuer listed the assets securing its senior secured bond in a separate appendix.
examples.zh: 示例发行人在单独的附录里列出了为「优先有担保物债券」提供担保的资产。

examples.en: Our tutor explained why the senior secured bond had priority over the subordinated note in the example.
examples.zh: 导师解释了为什么例子中的「优先有担保物债券」优先于次级票据受偿。

collocations: holders of a senior secured bond

words.enDefinition: a bond ranking as senior debt without a claim on specific pledged assets

examples.en: The example senior unsecured bond ranked above the subordinated debt in the same company's structure.
examples.zh: 同一家公司的示例结构里，「优先无担保物债券」的受偿顺位高于次级债务。

examples.en: The lecturer noted that the senior unsecured bond was not secured by a particular building.
examples.zh: 讲师指出，这只「优先无担保物债券」没有以某栋特定建筑作为担保。

collocations: rank of a senior unsecured bond

words.enDefinition: a bond whose holders rank behind specified senior creditors when payments or claims are prioritised

examples.en: We read the terms of the subordinated bond to see which obligations ranked ahead of it.
examples.zh: 我们读了「次级债券」的条款，看哪些债务的清偿顺位排在它前面。

examples.en: The model included a subordinated bond that would receive payment after the senior claims were met.
examples.zh: 模型里有一只「次级债券」，要等优先债权获清偿后才取得付款。

collocations: a subordinated bond ranks below senior debt

words.enDefinition: the rank of a debt claim relative to other claims for purposes of payment priority

examples.en: The case asked us to compare seniority across three bonds issued by the same company.
examples.zh: 案例让我们比较同一家公司发行的三只债券各自的「清偿优先顺位」。

examples.en: The adviser explained how the prospectus described the seniority of each note in the offering.
examples.zh: 顾问解释了募集文件如何描述各只票据的「清偿优先顺位」。

words.enDefinition: a Latin phrase meaning on equal footing, often used when obligations rank equally

examples.en: The lecturer pointed out that the two notes ranked pari passu in the example's payment structure.
examples.zh: 讲师指出，在该示例的付款结构中，两只票据处于「同等受偿顺位」。

examples.en: Our reading group discussed what pari passu meant for holders of the two unsecured notes.
examples.zh: 读书小组讨论了「同等受偿顺位」对两只无担保票据的持有人意味着什么。

words.enDefinition: a person or institution that holds a bond and has rights under its terms

examples.en: Each bondholder received a notice explaining the new date of the meeting in the case.
examples.zh: 案例中，每位「债券持有人」都收到了一份说明会议新日期的通知。

examples.en: I played a bondholder during our simulation and asked who was responsible for sending notices.
examples.zh: 模拟时我扮演「债券持有人」，询问谁负责发送通知。

words.enDefinition: an entity appointed to act for bondholders under the bond documents, with duties defined in those documents

examples.en: The sample indenture described when the bond trustee could send a notice on behalf of holders.
examples.zh: 示例契约说明，「债券受托人」可以在什么情况下代表持有人发通知。

examples.en: We checked the bond trustee information before reading the section about meetings and votes.
examples.zh: 我们先核对了「债券受托人」的信息，再读会议和投票章节。

words.enDefinition: a document defining bond terms and the duties of the appointed trustee, especially in UK and other trust-based issues

examples.en: We read the bond trust deed to see when the trustee could act for holders.
examples.zh: 我们读了「债券信托契约」，看受托人何时可以代表持有人行事。

examples.en: The bond trust deed described how holders would be notified of any change in terms.
examples.zh: 「债券信托契约」说明了更改条款时如何通知持有人。

collocations: duties under a bond trust deed
terms of a bond trust deed

words.enDefinition: a promise or restriction in the bond documents requiring or limiting particular actions by an issuer

examples.en: One bond covenant required the company to provide specified reports after the end of each year.
examples.zh: 有一项「债券契约约定」要求公司在每年年末后提供指定报告。

examples.en: Our tutor asked which bond covenant applied to the proposed sale in the fictional example.
examples.zh: 导师问，虚构案例中的拟议出售适用哪一项「债券契约约定」。

words.zhGloss: 规定必须采取行动的条款
words.enDefinition: a covenant requiring a borrower or issuer to take specified actions
acceptedZhAnswers: 规定必须采取行动的条款

examples.en: The affirmative covenant required the example issuer to send financial statements to the trustee regularly.
examples.zh: 「规定必须采取行动的条款」要求示例发行人定期向受托人发送财务报表。

examples.en: The tutor used an affirmative covenant to illustrate an obligation to do something under the agreement.
examples.zh: 导师用一项「规定必须采取行动的条款」说明，协议里可以约定必须做某件事。

collocations: an affirmative covenant to provide reports

words.enDefinition: a covenant prohibiting or limiting a borrower or issuer from taking particular actions

examples.en: The negative covenant limited the assets the example issuer could pledge for a new loan.
examples.zh: 「限制性承诺条款」限制了示例发行人可为新贷款提供哪些资产作为担保。

examples.en: Our class discussed why the negative covenant required an exception for certain routine business transactions.
examples.zh: 课堂讨论了为什么「限制性承诺条款」需要给某些日常商业交易留出例外。

words.enDefinition: a provision requiring a borrower to satisfy a financial test or limiting actions based on financial measures

examples.en: The sample financial covenant referred to the company's interest coverage ratio at the reporting date.
examples.zh: 示例「财务约束条款」提到了公司在报告日的利息保障倍数。

examples.en: We checked how the financial covenant defined debt before trying the exercise with sample figures.
examples.zh: 我们先看「财务约束条款」如何定义债务，再用示例数字做练习。

words.enDefinition: a covenant requiring a borrower to satisfy a test on a recurring basis, such as at reporting dates

examples.en: The lender tested the maintenance covenant at each quarterly reporting date in our fictional example.
examples.zh: 在虚构示例里，贷款方在每季度报告日都检验是否满足「定期维持型约束条款」。

examples.en: The tutor contrasted a maintenance covenant with a test that applied only when new debt was issued.
examples.zh: 导师把「定期维持型约束条款」与仅在新发债务时才适用的测试作了对比。

words.zhGloss: 特定行动触发的约束条款
words.enDefinition: a covenant tested when an issuer proposes a specified action, such as taking on additional debt
acceptedZhAnswers: 特定行动触发的约束条款

examples.en: The incurrence covenant mattered when the sample issuer considered raising more debt to expand production.
examples.zh: 示例发行人考虑加借债务以扩大生产时，「特定行动触发的约束条款」就起了作用。

examples.en: The notes explained why an incurrence covenant did not require the test every reporting period.
examples.zh: 讲义解释了为什么「特定行动触发的约束条款」不要求每个报告期都测试。

words.enDefinition: a failure to comply with a particular requirement or restriction in a debt agreement

examples.en: The case described a covenant breach after the issuer failed to provide the required statements.
examples.zh: 发行人没提供规定需要的报表，案例把这称为「违反契约约定」。

examples.en: The tutor asked whether the covenant breach in the example had been resolved by the company.
examples.zh: 导师问，案例公司是否已解决那次「违反契约约定」的问题。

words.enDefinition: an agreement by the relevant creditor or holders to waive a specified covenant requirement or breach

examples.en: The fictional borrower obtained a covenant waiver covering the missed reporting date in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中，虚构借款人拿到了一项涵盖错过报告日的「契约要求豁免」。

examples.en: Our lecturer explained why a covenant waiver for one breach did not remove the entire clause.
examples.zh: 讲师解释了为什么对一次违约的「契约要求豁免」不等于删除整个条款。

words.zhGloss: 距触发契约限值的余量
words.enDefinition: the margin between an actual or forecast financial measure and the limit in a covenant
acceptedZhAnswers: 距触发契约限值的余量

examples.en: The example showed less covenant headroom after the company's forecast interest expense increased for the quarter.
examples.zh: 公司的季度预测利息支出增加后，例子里的「距触发契约限值的余量」变小了。

examples.en: We calculated covenant headroom by comparing the forecast ratio with the limit in the agreement.
examples.zh: 我们把预测比率与协议里的限值作比较，算出「距触发契约限值的余量」。

words.zhGloss: 触发合同救济的违约事件
words.enDefinition: an event defined in a debt agreement that can trigger remedies, subject to any applicable conditions
acceptedZhAnswers: 触发合同救济的违约事件

examples.en: The fictional indenture listed nonpayment as a possible event of default after a specified period.
examples.zh: 虚构契约列明，不付款持续达到规定期限后，可能构成「触发合同救济的违约事件」。

examples.en: The lecturer explained that the event of default did not necessarily make every debt immediately payable.
examples.zh: 讲师解释了「触发合同救济的违约事件」并不一定会让所有债务立即到期。

collocations: notice of an event of default

words.enDefinition: a clause under which a covered default on other debt can trigger a default under this agreement

examples.en: In the case, our group reviewed the cross-default clause after another covered loan went into default.
examples.zh: 案例中的另一笔纳入条款的贷款发生违约后，我们小组查看了「交叉违约条款」。

examples.en: The sample cross-default clause defined which other debts were covered before listing possible consequences.
examples.zh: 示例「交叉违约条款」先定义涵盖的其他债务，再列出可能的后果。

words.enDefinition: a clause triggered when specified other debt is declared due early after a default

examples.en: The lawyer in the case explained when the cross-acceleration clause would apply to the separate note.
examples.zh: 案例中的律师说明了「交叉加速到期条款」会在什么情况下适用于另一只票据。

examples.en: Our tutor used the cross-acceleration clause to distinguish a missed payment from formally accelerating a loan.
examples.zh: 导师用「交叉加速到期条款」区分了漏还一笔款和正式宣布贷款提前到期。

words.enDefinition: a provision allowing an unpaid balance to become due earlier when specified conditions are met

examples.en: The agreement's acceleration clause described when the lender could demand the remaining amount before maturity.
examples.zh: 协议的「加速到期条款」说明了贷款方何时能在期限届满前要求还清余额。

examples.en: We identified the acceleration clause during a classroom exercise on the consequences of a default.
examples.zh: 课堂练习讨论违约后果时，我们找出了「加速到期条款」。

words.enDefinition: a bondholder right to require repurchase after a change of control if the stated conditions are met

examples.en: The terms of the change-of-control put identified the events that might give holders a repurchase right.
examples.zh: 「控制权变更回售权」条款列出了哪些事件可能让持有人有权要求回购。

examples.en: We discussed a change-of-control put after the fictional issuer agreed to be acquired by another company.
examples.zh: 虚构发行人同意被另一家公司收购后，我们讨论了「控制权变更回售权」。

words.enDefinition: a formal request for bondholders to consent to proposed changes or other actions under the bond documents

examples.en: The issuer sent a consent solicitation explaining its proposed change to the reporting deadline.
examples.zh: 发行人发出「征求债券持有人同意」的文件，解释了拟议的报告截止日期变更。

examples.en: We counted the responses to the sample consent solicitation during the classroom exercise on bond terms.
examples.zh: 在有关债券条款的课堂练习中，我们统计了「征求债券持有人同意」样本的回复。

words.enDefinition: a change to the terms or provisions of a bond indenture

examples.en: The sample indenture amendment changed one reporting date while leaving the coupon payment schedule intact.
examples.zh: 示例「债券契约修订」调整了一处报告日，票息支付安排保持原样。

examples.en: The lecturer noted that the indenture amendment required the type of approval specified in the contract.
examples.zh: 讲师指出，「债券契约修订」需要获得合同规定的那种批准。

words.enDefinition: the overall set of collateral, security interests and related documents supporting a financing arrangement

examples.en: The sample security package included a pledge over equipment and an assignment of specified receivables.
examples.zh: 示例「债务担保组合」包含以设备设定担保和转让指定应收款。

examples.en: Our group compared the security package with the general promise to pay in a separate note.
examples.zh: 我们小组把「债务担保组合」与另一只票据中的一般付款承诺作了比较。

words.enDefinition: the extent to which the value of pledged assets covers the amount of debt they secure

examples.en: The analyst measured collateral coverage using the assessed value of the equipment listed in the example.
examples.zh: 分析人员用示例所列设备的评估值衡量「担保物价值覆盖程度」。

examples.en: We compared collateral coverage before and after the appraised value of the property was reduced.
examples.zh: 我们比较了物业估值调低前后的「担保物价值覆盖程度」。

words.enDefinition: a bond whose payments are guaranteed by another party under specified terms

examples.en: The sample guaranteed bond named a parent company as guarantor on the cover of the document.
examples.zh: 示例「保证人担保债券」在文件封面注明，一家母公司是保证人。

examples.en: The tutor asked whose separate promise to pay supported the guaranteed bond in the example.
examples.zh: 导师问，示例中的「保证人担保债券」由谁另行承诺偿付。

words.enDefinition: a bond that the issuer may redeem before maturity under the terms of the issue

examples.en: We read the dates on the callable bond before comparing it with a noncallable issue.
examples.zh: 我们先读「可提前赎回债券」上的日期，再把它和不可提前赎回的债券作比较。

examples.en: The lecturer used a callable bond to show how an issuer could repay debt before maturity.
examples.zh: 讲师用「可提前赎回债券」说明发行人可以怎样在到期前清偿债务。

words.enDefinition: a bond whose holder can require the issuer to buy it back at times or under conditions specified in the terms

examples.en: The student compared a puttable bond with one that only the issuer could redeem early.
examples.zh: 学生把「可回售债券」与只有发行人能提前赎回的债券作了比较。

examples.en: We found the first holder option date for the puttable bond in the example's terms.
examples.zh: 我们在示例条款中找到了这只「可回售债券」持有人首次可以要求回购的日期。

words.enDefinition: a bond that can be converted into another security, typically the issuer's shares, under specified terms

examples.en: The class reviewed a convertible bond that could be converted into shares of the same company.
examples.zh: 课堂上我们看了一只「可转换债券」，它可以换成同一家公司的股票。

examples.en: The terms of the convertible bond gave the dates when holders could exercise the conversion right.
examples.zh: 「可转换债券」条款列出了持有人可行使转换权的日期。

collocations: convert a convertible bond into shares

words.enDefinition: a bond that can be exchanged for another company's shares under specified terms

examples.en: The exercise used an exchangeable bond linked to shares the fictional issuer held in another company.
examples.zh: 练习选了一只「可交换债券」，对应虚构发行人持有的另一家公司股份。

examples.en: The terms explained how the exchangeable bond differed from a note convertible into the issuer's shares.
examples.zh: 条款解释了「可交换债券」与可换成发行人自身股票的票据有何不同。

words.enDefinition: a security recorded electronically in accounts without delivery of a physical certificate

examples.en: The guide explained how a book-entry security appeared on a statement from the securities account.
examples.zh: 指南解释了「簿记式证券」怎样显示在证券账户对账单上。

examples.en: We compared the record for a book-entry security with an image of an old certificate.
examples.zh: 我们把「簿记式证券」的记录与一张旧式实物凭证的图片作了比较。

words.enDefinition: a bond whose principal is repaid in a single payment at maturity

examples.en: The cash-flow schedule for the bullet bond showed all principal due on the final date.
examples.zh: 「到期一次还本债券」的现金流表显示，全部本金在最后一天到期。

examples.en: We compared the bullet bond with a bond that repaid principal in several scheduled amounts.
examples.zh: 我们把「到期一次还本债券」与分几期偿还本金的债券作了比较。

words.enDefinition: the spread specified in bond terms to add to the benchmark yield used in a make-whole redemption calculation

examples.en: The indenture listed the make-whole spread beside the method for selecting a benchmark Treasury.
examples.zh: 这份债券契约把「补偿赎回计价利差」列在美国基准国债的选取方法旁。

examples.en: We added the make-whole spread to the benchmark yield before discounting the remaining scheduled payments.
examples.zh: 我们把「补偿赎回计价利差」加到基准收益率上，再折算剩余的约定付款。

collocations: add a make-whole spread to the benchmark yield

words.enDefinition: a bond with no scheduled maturity date, though the issuer may have a right to redeem it

examples.en: The terms of the perpetual bond listed call dates but showed no fixed maturity date.
examples.zh: 「永续债券」的条款列出了可赎回日期，没有列固定到期日。

examples.en: The tutor asked whether the perpetual bond would have to be redeemed at its first call date.
examples.zh: 导师问，「永续债券」是否必须在首次可赎回日期赎回。

words.enDefinition: a debt security whose interest rate is periodically reset using a specified reference or formula

examples.en: The floating-rate note used a benchmark rate plus a spread listed in its terms.
examples.zh: 「浮动利率票据」采用基准利率加条款里所列的利差。

examples.en: We read the floating-rate note example before calculating the interest for the next payment period.
examples.zh: 我们先看「浮动利率票据」的例子，再算下一付款期的利息。

words.enDefinition: a debt security whose stated coupon rate stays the same through its life

examples.en: The fixed-rate note paid interest at the same coupon rate in each period of the example.
examples.zh: 例中的「固定利率票据」每期都按相同的票面利率付息。

examples.en: The tutor asked us to compare a fixed-rate note with a note linked to a benchmark.
examples.zh: 导师要求我们比较「固定利率票据」与挂钩基准利率的票据。

words.enDefinition: a debt security whose coupon rate rises on stated dates or when a specified condition occurs

examples.en: The step-up note in the example paid a higher rate after three years under its terms.
examples.zh: 例中的「票息递升票据」按条款约定，在三年后按更高利率付息。

examples.en: Our worksheet listed the dates when the coupon on the step-up note would change.
examples.zh: 练习表列出了「票息递升票据」票息会在哪些日期变动。

collocations: coupon schedule of a step-up note

words.enDefinition: a bond with no periodic coupon payments, usually issued below its redemption value

examples.en: We priced a zero-coupon bond by finding the present value of its single maturity payment.
examples.zh: 我们计算「零息债券」唯一一笔到期付款的现值，以得出债券价格。

examples.en: The zero-coupon bond appeared in the table without any interest payments before its maturity.
examples.zh: 表中的「零息债券」在到期之前没有列出任何利息付款。

words.enDefinition: a bond whose payments or principal are adjusted using a specified inflation index

examples.en: The prospectus showed how the principal of the inflation-linked bond changed with the named index.
examples.zh: 募集文件展示了「通胀挂钩债券」的本金怎样随注明的指数变化。

examples.en: Our class compared an inflation-linked bond with a conventional bond from the same government.
examples.zh: 我们班比较了同一政府发行的「通胀挂钩债券」和普通债券。

words.enDefinition: US Treasury securities whose principal is adjusted using a consumer price index

examples.en: Our worksheet used Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities to show how an index adjustment affects principal.
examples.zh: 练习表用「美国通胀保值国债」说明指数调整会怎样影响本金。

examples.en: The guide discussed Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities separately from conventional fixed-principal Treasury notes and bonds.
examples.zh: 指南把「美国通胀保值国债」和财政部发行的固定本金票据、债券分开介绍。

words.enDefinition: a short-term US Treasury security that ordinarily has no periodic interest payments

examples.en: The lecturer used a Treasury bill to illustrate the difference between issue price and face value.
examples.zh: 讲师用一只「美国短期国库券」说明发行价格与面值的区别。

examples.en: We looked up the maturity of the Treasury bill listed in the practice auction announcement.
examples.zh: 我们查看了练习用拍卖公告所列「美国短期国库券」什么时候到期。

words.enDefinition: a US Treasury security issued with a term of two to ten years and fixed coupon payments

examples.en: The auction notice described a five-year Treasury note and gave both auction and issue dates.
examples.zh: 拍卖通知介绍了一只五年期「美国中期国债」，并列出拍卖与发行日期。

examples.en: Our tutor compared the cash flows of a Treasury note and a short-term Treasury bill.
examples.zh: 导师比较了「美国中期国债」与短期国库券的现金流。

words.enDefinition: US Treasury debt instruments that can be bought and sold in the secondary market

examples.en: Our class used Treasury marketable securities to illustrate how an auction differs from secondary trading.
examples.zh: 课堂用「可交易美国国债」说明拍卖与二级市场交易的区别。

examples.en: The guide separated Treasury marketable securities from the savings bonds it described later on.
examples.zh: 指南把「可交易美国国债」与后文介绍的储蓄国债分开说明。

words.zhGloss: 美国拆分本金或利息的国债
words.enDefinition: US Treasury zero-coupon securities created by separating payments on eligible notes, bonds or Treasury Inflation-Protected Securities
acceptedZhAnswers: 美国拆分本金或利息的国债

examples.en: The lecturer showed how STRIPS could represent separate payments from one original Treasury security.
examples.zh: 讲师演示了「美国拆分本金或利息的国债」怎样对应同一只原始国债的各笔付款。

examples.en: Our table listed several STRIPS with different maturity dates but no regular coupon payments.
examples.zh: 我们的表列了几只「美国拆分本金或利息的国债」，到期日不同，都无定期票息。

words.enDefinition: a government savings security that is generally intended for individuals and may be nonmarketable

examples.en: The Treasury guide distinguished a savings bond from the securities sold at regular Treasury auctions.
examples.zh: 财政部指南把「储蓄国债」与通过常规国债拍卖出售的证券区分开。

examples.en: The class discussed why the example savings bond could not be sold to another investor.
examples.zh: 课堂讨论了为什么例中的「储蓄国债」不能在市场上卖给另一位投资者。

words.enDefinition: a US municipal bond backed by the issuer's general credit and, subject to terms, taxing power

examples.en: The workbook compared a general obligation bond with a bond paid from a specific facility's revenue.
examples.zh: 练习册比较了「一般责任市政债券」和以特定设施收入还款的债券。

examples.en: The adviser explained which promise supported the general obligation bond in the municipal financing example.
examples.zh: 顾问解释了市政融资示例中哪项付款承诺支持这只「一般责任市政债券」。

collocations: holders of a general obligation bond

words.enDefinition: a bond rated below investment grade, or with comparable credit risk, generally offering a higher yield

examples.en: The fund document identified the issue as a high-yield bond and discussed the issuer's credit risk.
examples.zh: 基金文件称这是一只「高收益债券」，还讨论了发行人的信用风险。

examples.en: The lecturer noted that the label high-yield bond referred to the credit category in the table.
examples.zh: 讲师指出，表中的「高收益债券」是信用类别标签。

collocations: credit risk of a high-yield bond

words.enDefinition: a bond with a credit rating that meets an agency's threshold for investment grade

examples.en: The prospectus listed an investment-grade bond beside an issue rated below that agency's applicable cutoff.
examples.zh: 募集文件把一只「投资级债券」和低于该评级机构门槛的债券并排列出。

examples.en: Our tutor said an investment-grade bond could still be affected by changing rates and issuer risk.
examples.zh: 导师说，「投资级债券」仍可能受利率变化和发行人风险影响。

words.zhGloss: 降至非投资级的原投资级债券
words.enDefinition: a bond or issuer downgraded from investment grade to below investment grade
acceptedZhAnswers: 降至非投资级的原投资级债券

examples.en: The sample bond became a fallen angel after its rating moved below the investment-grade threshold.
examples.zh: 示例债券评级降到投资级门槛以下，成为「降至非投资级的原投资级债券」。

examples.en: Our tutor asked which rating change would make the note a fallen angel in the table.
examples.zh: 导师问，表中的票据会在哪种评级变化后成为「降至非投资级的原投资级债券」。

words.zhGloss: 升至投资级的原非投资级债券
words.enDefinition: a bond or issuer upgraded from below investment grade to investment grade
acceptedZhAnswers: 升至投资级的原非投资级债券

examples.en: The worksheet called the bond a rising star after the agency raised it to investment grade.
examples.zh: 评级机构把债券升至投资级后，练习表称它为「升至投资级的原非投资级债券」。

examples.en: We compared the rising star with an issuer that had stayed within the same rating category.
examples.zh: 我们把这只「升至投资级的原非投资级债券」与评级类别没变的发行人作了比较。

words.enDefinition: a decision by a rating agency to assign a lower credit rating to an issuer or issue

examples.en: The agency announced the rating downgrade after the company published a revised forecast for the year.
examples.zh: 公司公布修改后的年度预测后，评级机构宣布对债券「下调评级」。

examples.en: We discussed the reasons for the rating downgrade using the fictional agency notice in class.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们通过虚构评级机构的通知讨论了「评级下调」的原因。

words.enDefinition: a decision by a rating agency to assign a higher credit rating to an issuer or issue

examples.en: The company's rating upgrade followed a review of its ability to repay debt in the case.
examples.zh: 案例中，在审查公司的偿债能力后作出了「评级上调」。

examples.en: The sample announcement explained why the rating upgrade applied to some issues and not others.
examples.zh: 样本公告解释了为什么「评级上调」适用于部分债券，其他债券维持原评级。

words.enDefinition: a rating agency's indication of the possible direction of a rating over a stated time horizon

examples.en: The rating outlook changed in the example even though the rating itself remained the same.
examples.zh: 虽然评级本身保持原样，例子中的「评级展望」发生了变化。

examples.en: Our tutor asked where the rating outlook appeared in the agency's release about the issuer.
examples.zh: 导师问，评级机构关于发行人的公告里，「评级展望」出现在什么地方。

words.enDefinition: a rating outlook indicating that the credit rating may be lowered within the relevant horizon

examples.en: The sample release retained the current rating but attached a negative outlook to the issuer.
examples.zh: 样本公告保留了当前评级，但将发行人列为「负面评级展望」。

examples.en: Our lecturer explained that a negative outlook describes a possible direction for a future rating change.
examples.zh: 讲师解释了「负面评级展望」说明的是未来评级变化的一种可能方向。

collocations: credit rating with a negative outlook

words.enDefinition: a rating outlook indicating that the credit rating may be raised within the relevant horizon

examples.en: The fictional issuer received a positive outlook after the agency assessed its improving finances.
examples.zh: 评级机构评估财务状况有所改善后，虚构发行人的评级被赋予「正面评级展望」。

examples.en: The tutor asked why the positive outlook was shown separately from the unchanged bond rating.
examples.zh: 导师问，为什么「正面评级展望」与没有变化的债券评级分开显示。

words.enDefinition: a rating outlook indicating that the rating is unlikely to change within the relevant horizon

examples.en: The rating agency's case report kept a stable outlook on the fictional company's long-term debt.
examples.zh: 案例中的评级机构报告维持了虚构公司长期债务的「稳定评级展望」。

examples.en: We discussed why a stable outlook was listed even though the issue could still lose value.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了为什么即使债券仍可能贬值，文件里也列出「稳定评级展望」。

words.enDefinition: a designation indicating a focused review that may result in a near-term rating action

examples.en: The agency placed the issuer on rating watch after a proposed sale appeared in the case.
examples.zh: 案例中出现拟议的出售交易后，机构把发行人列入「评级观察」。

examples.en: Our tutor used rating watch to describe a reassessment prompted by the issuer's proposed sale.
examples.zh: 导师用「评级观察」来说明，发行人提出出售计划后引发的评级重新审查。

collocations: place an issuer on rating watch
remove a rating from rating watch

words.enDefinition: a credit rating assessing an issuer's general capacity and willingness to meet financial obligations

examples.en: The agency table displayed an issuer rating before listing separate ratings for the company's two bonds.
examples.zh: 评级机构的表上先显示「发行人信用评级」，再列公司两只债券各自的评级。

examples.en: The tutor explained why the issuer rating assessed the company rather than the terms of one bond.
examples.zh: 导师解释了为什么「发行人信用评级」评估的是公司整体，单只债券的条款另看。

words.enDefinition: a credit rating for a particular debt obligation that may reflect its own terms and rank

examples.en: The issue rating differed from the company's general credit rating because the note ranked lower.
examples.zh: 这只票据受偿顺位较低，「单项债券信用评级」便与公司的整体信用评级不同。

examples.en: We checked the issue rating for the unsecured notes in the agency's example table.
examples.zh: 我们查看了评级机构示例表中无担保票据的「单项债券信用评级」。

collocations: an issue rating on a bond

words.zhGloss: 不同机构给出的分歧评级
words.enDefinition: a situation in which different agencies assign different credit ratings to the same issuer or issue
acceptedZhAnswers: 不同机构给出的分歧评级

examples.en: The split rating appeared because one agency placed the debt above the investment-grade cutoff and one below.
examples.zh: 一家机构把债务评在投资级门槛以上，另一家评在以下，形成「不同机构给出的分歧评级」。

examples.en: The tutor asked how the split rating would be displayed in the fund's sample holdings report.
examples.zh: 导师问，基金持仓样本报告会怎样显示「不同机构给出的分歧评级」。

collocations: a bond with a split rating

words.enDefinition: one step between adjacent grades on a credit rating agency's scale

examples.en: The issuer moved up by one rating notch after the agency announced the results of its review.
examples.zh: 机构公布复核结果后，发行人提高了一个「评级档位」。

examples.en: Our tutor explained what counted as a rating notch on the scale printed in the notes.
examples.zh: 导师解释了讲义所印评级刻度上，怎样算一个「评级档位」。

collocations: a change of one rating notch

words.enDefinition: a movement of an issuer or obligation from one credit rating category to another over time

examples.en: The worksheet used credit migration to compare changes in rating groups across several annual observations.
examples.zh: 练习表通过「信用评级迁移」比较了连续几年各评级类别的变化。

examples.en: Our tutor distinguished credit migration from changes in the market price of the same notes.
examples.zh: 导师把「信用评级迁移」与同一批票据市场价格的变化作了区分。

words.enDefinition: a table showing probabilities or observed frequencies of moving between rating categories over a period

examples.en: We used a rating transition matrix to find how often issuers stayed in the same grade.
examples.zh: 我们用「评级迁移矩阵」查看发行人维持原评级的频率。

examples.en: The rating transition matrix included a column for issuers that defaulted during the observation period.
examples.zh: 「评级迁移矩阵」有一列记录在观察期内发生违约的发行人。

words.enDefinition: the estimated chance that a borrower or specified obligation will default over a stated period

examples.en: The model reported the probability of default over one year for each fictional borrower in the exercise.
examples.zh: 模型报告了练习中每个虚构借款人一年内的「违约概率」。

examples.en: We used the same time horizon when comparing each borrower's estimated probability of default.
examples.zh: 我们先统一了时间区间，再比较表中各借款人的估计「违约概率」。

words.enDefinition: the share of exposure expected to be lost if the borrower defaults, after considering recoveries

examples.en: We compared loss given default in two examples with different values for the pledged assets.
examples.zh: 我们比较了担保物价值不同的两个示例中的「违约损失率」。

examples.en: The tutor asked why the estimated loss given default was shown as a percentage, not a currency amount.
examples.zh: 导师问，为什么估算的「违约损失率」用百分比表示，而不是货币金额。

words.enDefinition: the total amount exposed to loss at the time a borrower or counterparty defaults

examples.en: The exercise set exposure at default separately from the proportion the creditor expected to lose.
examples.zh: 练习把「违约风险敞口」和债权人预期损失的比例分开设定。

examples.en: We calculated exposure at default before applying the loss rate from the classroom example table.
examples.zh: 我们先计算「违约风险敞口」，再应用课堂示例表里的损失率。

collocations: exposure at default for a loan

words.enDefinition: the proportion of a defaulted exposure that creditors recover, sometimes measured net of costs or discounted

examples.en: The analyst compared the recovery rate for two defaulted claims after estimating the costs of collection.
examples.zh: 分析人员估算回收成本后，比较了两笔违约债权的「违约债权回收率」。

examples.en: Our tutor showed how the assumed recovery rate affected the estimated loss on the bond.
examples.zh: 导师演示了假定的「违约债权回收率」会怎样影响债券损失估计值。

words.enDefinition: a bond for which a default has occurred under its terms

examples.en: The sample portfolio listed the defaulted bond separately from other bonds with low credit ratings.
examples.zh: 样本组合把「已违约债券」和其他低评级债券分开列出。

examples.en: We read the notice for the defaulted bond to learn which scheduled payment had been missed.
examples.zh: 我们查看「已违约债券」的通知，了解哪笔预定付款没有支付。

words.enDefinition: a bond trading at levels associated with serious financial trouble or heightened default risk

examples.en: Our tutor described the distressed bond as risky even though the issuer was still paying coupons.
examples.zh: 导师说，尽管发行人仍在付息，这只「困境债券」风险也很高。

examples.en: The fictional price list marked one distressed bond separately from debt that had already defaulted.
examples.zh: 虚构价格表把一只「困境债券」与已经违约的债务分开标记。

words.enDefinition: a yield difference between debt with credit risk and a comparable benchmark or lower-risk debt

examples.en: The chart showed a wider credit spread for the corporate bond than for its peers.
examples.zh: 图表显示，这只公司债券的「信用利差」比同类债券更大。

examples.en: We calculated the credit spread after choosing a government bond of similar maturity as the benchmark.
examples.zh: 我们选了一只到期时间相近的国债作为基准，然后计算「信用利差」。

words.enDefinition: an increase in the difference between a security's yield and the yield used as its benchmark

examples.en: The risk report showed spread widening even though the benchmark government yield had hardly changed.
examples.zh: 虽然作为基准的国债收益率几乎没变，风险报告还是显示了「利差扩大」。

examples.en: Our class compared the effect of spread widening on two bonds with different durations.
examples.zh: 课堂比较了「利差扩大」对两只久期不同的债券有何影响。

words.enDefinition: a decrease in the difference between a security's yield and the yield used as its benchmark

examples.en: The example linked spread tightening to a lower yield on the note relative to its benchmark.
examples.zh: 例子把「利差收窄」和该票据相对基准的收益率下降联系起来。

examples.en: The tutor asked whether spread tightening had occurred after the two yields moved closer together.
examples.zh: 两项收益率变得更接近后，导师问有没有发生「利差收窄」。

words.enDefinition: a model-based spread over benchmark rates after accounting for embedded options in a bond

examples.en: We used the option-adjusted spread to compare the sample callable bond with a similar noncallable issue.
examples.zh: 我们用「期权调整利差」比较样本可赎回债券与一只类似的不可赎回债券。

examples.en: The analyst explained why the option-adjusted spread changed when the assumed interest rate volatility changed.
examples.zh: 分析人员解释了为什么假定的利率波动率改变后，「期权调整利差」也会变化。

words.enDefinition: a constant spread added to a benchmark spot curve so discounted bond payments match the market price

examples.en: Our worksheet solved for the zero-volatility spread using the benchmark spot rates and the stated payments.
examples.zh: 练习表用基准即期利率与约定付款额求出了「零波动率利差」。

examples.en: The tutor explained how the zero-volatility spread differed from a spread accounting for an embedded option.
examples.zh: 导师解释了「零波动率利差」与考虑内嵌期权的利差有何不同。

collocations: zero-volatility spread over the spot curve

words.enDefinition: the spread over an assumed reference rate that makes the present value of a floating-rate note's projected payments equal its price

examples.en: The auction results showed the discount margin accepted for the new Treasury floating-rate note.
examples.zh: 示例拍卖结果显示了新发财政部浮动利率票据确定的「浮息票据折现利差」。

examples.en: We distinguished the discount margin from the spread already specified in a note's coupon formula.
examples.zh: 我们区分了「浮息票据折现利差」和票据票息公式里已经约定的利差。

words.enDefinition: an externally specified interest rate used as the starting point for calculating another rate

examples.en: The floating-rate note used a reference rate plus the margin printed in the terms.
examples.zh: 「参考利率」与条款印出的利差相加，得出浮动利率票据的利率。

examples.en: We found the reference rate in the sample document before checking the interest reset dates.
examples.zh: 我们先在样本文件里找到「参考利率」，再核对利率重设日期。

collocations: link interest to a reference rate

words.enDefinition: a margin added to or subtracted from a reference rate to determine a floating coupon

examples.en: The terms specified a coupon spread to be added to the reference rate at each reset.
examples.zh: 条款约定，每次重设利率时，都在参考利率上加上「票息利差」。

examples.en: We checked whether the coupon spread stayed fixed when the note's reference rate moved higher.
examples.zh: 票据的参考利率走高时，我们检查了「票息利差」是否保持原值。

collocations: coupon spread over the reference rate

words.enDefinition: a recalculation of a floating interest rate under the applicable formula and timing rules

examples.en: The next interest rate reset would use the new reference rate published after the holiday.
examples.zh: 下一次「利率重设」会使用假期后公布的新参考利率。

examples.en: The workbook showed how an interest rate reset changed the coupon payment for the following quarter.
examples.zh: 练习册展示了一次「利率重设」如何改变下一季度的票息付款。

words.enDefinition: the date on which a floating rate is recalculated or takes effect according to the instrument's terms

examples.en: I marked the reset date before calculating which reference rate applied in the example worksheet.
examples.zh: 我标了「利率重设日」，然后才算练习表的案例采用哪项参考利率。

examples.en: The example's reset date was listed separately from the day holders received their scheduled interest.
examples.zh: 例子把「利率重设日」与持有人收到预定利息的日期分开列出。

words.enDefinition: the lowest coupon rate that can apply under the terms of a variable-rate instrument

examples.en: The coupon floor came into effect when the reference rate fell in the sample calculation.
examples.zh: 示例计算中参考利率下降后，「票面利率下限」开始起作用。

examples.en: The prospectus placed the coupon floor beside a separate provision setting the highest rate allowed.
examples.zh: 募集文件把「票面利率下限」和规定最高利率的条款并排列出。

words.enDefinition: the highest coupon rate permitted by the terms of a variable-rate instrument

examples.en: The sample note reached its coupon cap after the reference rate rose during the year.
examples.zh: 示例票据的参考利率在年内上涨后，票面利率触及「票面利率上限」。

examples.en: We found the coupon cap in the same section of the prospectus as the reference rate.
examples.zh: 我们在募集文件介绍参考利率的那个章节，找到了「票面利率上限」。

words.enDefinition: a date specified for paying interest on a loan or debt security

examples.en: The schedule listed the next interest payment date below the information about the annual coupon rate.
examples.zh: 还款表在年度票面利率信息下方列出了下一个「利息支付日」。

examples.en: We checked the interest payment date because it fell after the end of our comparison period.
examples.zh: 我们查了「利息支付日」，因为它落在比较期结束以后。

words.enDefinition: an initial or final coupon period whose length differs from a regular period in the schedule

examples.en: The sample bond started with a stub coupon period shorter than its ordinary payment intervals.
examples.zh: 示例债券一开始有一个「不规则票息期」，比常规付款间隔短。

examples.en: The tutor showed how the stub coupon period affected the amount of the first interest payment.
examples.zh: 导师演示了「不规则票息期」会怎样影响第一笔利息付款金额。

collocations: calculate interest for a stub coupon period
bond with a stub coupon period

words.enDefinition: the rule used to calculate the fraction of a year represented by an interest period

examples.en: We checked the day-count convention before calculating interest for the first coupon period in the example.
examples.zh: 计算示例首个票息期的利息之前，我们先查看了「计息天数惯例」。

examples.en: The class compared two results obtained by applying a different day-count convention to the same dates.
examples.zh: 课堂比较了两种「计息天数惯例」对同一组日期算出的结果。

words.enDefinition: a family of day-count methods using actual calendar days, with the year fraction defined by the particular version

examples.en: The terms named an actual/actual convention for calculating the interest accruing between the two dates.
examples.zh: 条款规定用「实际天数计息惯例」计算这两个日期之间应计的利息。

examples.en: The tutor asked which version of actual/actual the worksheet used before we compared our answers.
examples.zh: 导师让我们先看练习表用的是哪种「实际天数计息惯例」，再比较答案。

words.enDefinition: a family of day-count methods that use a 30-day month and 360-day year, with different end-date rules

examples.en: The note uses a 30/360 day-count convention to calculate interest for the first period.
examples.zh: 这只票据采用「按月30天年360天计息」的惯例计算首期利息。

examples.en: Our tutor compared versions of the 30/360 day-count convention to show why month-end dates mattered.
examples.zh: 导师比较了不同版本的「按月30天年360天计息」惯例，说明为什么月末日期重要。

words.enDefinition: the price of a bond excluding accrued interest

examples.en: The clean price in the example was lower than the amount paid at settlement.
examples.zh: 例中的「债券净价」比结算时支付的金额低。

examples.en: We added the accrued interest to the clean price to calculate the total payable.
examples.zh: 我们把应计利息加到「债券净价」上，算出了应付总额。

words.enDefinition: the price of a bond including accrued interest

examples.en: The dirty price included the interest that had built up since the last scheduled coupon date.
examples.zh: 「债券全价」包含上一个预定付息日之后已经累计的利息。

examples.en: The tutor placed the dirty price next to the quoted clean price on the worksheet.
examples.zh: 导师把「债券全价」和报价中的净价并排写在练习表上。

words.enDefinition: a bond whose quoted or issue price is equal to its face value

examples.en: The first example showed a bond at par before introducing a bond priced above face value.
examples.zh: 第一个例子先展示「按面值计价的债券」，随后才引入价格高于面值的债券。

examples.en: Our tutor used a bond at par to explain why price and face value sometimes match.
examples.zh: 导师用「按面值计价的债券」说明价格和面值为什么有时相同。

words.enDefinition: describes a bond trading at a price higher than its face value

examples.en: The example showed a bond trading above par when its fixed coupon exceeded the comparable market yield.
examples.zh: 示例债券固定票息率高于可比市场收益率时，「交易价高于面值」。

examples.en: We noted which bond was trading above par before comparing the prices and payment schedules.
examples.zh: 我们先标出哪只债券「交易价高于面值」，再比较价格和付款安排。

words.enDefinition: describes a bond trading at a price lower than its face value

examples.en: We identified the note trading below par by comparing its quoted price with its face value.
examples.zh: 我们把报价和面值一比，找出了哪只票据「交易价低于面值」。

examples.en: A note trading below par can reflect concern about the issuer's ability to repay.
examples.zh: 票据「交易价低于面值」，可能反映市场担忧发行人的偿债能力。

words.enDefinition: the amount by which certain debt is issued below the amount repayable at maturity

examples.en: The note's original issue discount was shown next to the amount due at maturity in the example.
examples.zh: 示例在票据到期应付金额旁列了「原始发行折价」。

examples.en: The lecturer distinguished the original issue discount from a later fall in the bond's market price.
examples.zh: 讲师区分了「原始发行折价」与后来债券市场价格的下跌。

collocations: issue debt with original issue discount

words.enDefinition: the excess of the issue price of a security above its face value

examples.en: The exercise used a small issue premium for the bond because it was issued above face value.
examples.zh: 练习把债券设为略有「发行溢价」，因为发行价高于面值。

examples.en: We recorded the issue premium separately when comparing proceeds from the two fictional bond issues.
examples.zh: 比较两笔虚构债券发行所得时，我们把「发行溢价」单独记了下来。

collocations: a bond issued at an issue premium

words.enDefinition: repayment or redemption of a bond at its face value

examples.en: The terms allowed redemption at par after the first three years of the fictional issue.
examples.zh: 虚构发行的条款规定，最初三年过后可以「按面值赎回」。

examples.en: We compared redemption at par with a separate case in which the issuer paid a premium.
examples.zh: 我们把「按面值赎回」和发行人支付溢价的另一个例子作了比较。

words.enDefinition: an amount paid above face value when a bond is redeemed under its terms

examples.en: The redemption premium made the total repayment higher than the face amount in the example.
examples.zh: 示例中的「赎回溢价」使偿付总额高于面值。

examples.en: We located the redemption premium in the table before checking which call date it covered.
examples.zh: 我们先在表里找到「赎回溢价」，再核对它适用于哪个可赎回日期。

words.enDefinition: the earliest date when an issuer can use the relevant call provision to redeem a bond

examples.en: The group marked the first call date before reading when the note would otherwise mature.
examples.zh: 我们小组先标出「首个可赎回日」，再看票据在正常情况下何时到期。

examples.en: Our tutor asked whether the issuer had to act on the first call date in the example.
examples.zh: 导师问，示例里的发行人是否必须在「首个可赎回日」采取行动。

collocations: redeem on the first call date

words.enDefinition: a schedule of dates or periods and associated prices at which a bond may be called

examples.en: The call schedule showed a lower redemption price later in the life of the bond.
examples.zh: 「赎回日期与价格表」显示，债券存续到后期时的赎回价格更低。

examples.en: We checked the call schedule while comparing two hypothetical notes with the same maturity date.
examples.zh: 我们比较到期日相同的两只假设票据时，查了「赎回日期与价格表」。

collocations: find a price on the call schedule

words.enDefinition: terms limiting when or how the issuer may call a bond before maturity

examples.en: The sample note offered call protection for the early years before regular call dates began.
examples.zh: 在常规可赎回日期开始之前，样本票据最初几年有「限制提前赎回的保护」。

examples.en: The lecturer explained how call protection affected the expected timing of payments in the example.
examples.zh: 讲师解释了示例中的「限制提前赎回的保护」会怎样影响预期付款时间。

words.zhGloss: 不可按常规条款提前赎回的期间
words.enDefinition: a period when the issuer cannot exercise a specified option to redeem the bond early
acceptedZhAnswers: 不可按常规条款提前赎回的期间

examples.en: The bond had a three-year non-call period before the first ordinary issuer call was permitted.
examples.zh: 这只债券有三年的「不可按常规条款提前赎回的期间」，之后才允许发行人按常规条款首次赎回。

examples.en: The tutor asked when the non-call period ended under the terms shown in the example.
examples.zh: 导师问，按示例中的条款，「不可按常规条款提前赎回的期间」何时结束。

words.enDefinition: a redemption the issuer may choose to make under the stated conditions

examples.en: The terms included optional redemption after a specified date at the price shown in the table.
examples.zh: 条款包括在指定日期后按表列价格进行「选择性赎回」的安排。

examples.en: We discussed whether optional redemption changed the cash flows we needed to model for the exercise.
examples.zh: 我们讨论了「选择性赎回」是否会改变练习中需要模拟的现金流。

collocations: exercise a right of optional redemption

words.zhGloss: 因特定特殊事件而赎回
words.enDefinition: early redemption permitted or required after certain exceptional events stated in the bond terms
acceptedZhAnswers: 因特定特殊事件而赎回

examples.en: The document described extraordinary redemption if the insured facility suffered severe damage in the example.
examples.zh: 文件说明了示例中受保设施严重受损时「因特定特殊事件而赎回」的安排。

examples.en: The tutor compared extraordinary redemption with a routine option to call the bond on specific dates.
examples.zh: 导师比较了「因特定特殊事件而赎回」与在特定日期常规赎回债券的权利。

words.enDefinition: redemption of some bonds on a schedule using funds set aside as required by the bond terms

examples.en: The example used sinking fund redemption to repay part of the issue before final maturity.
examples.zh: 示例用「偿债基金分期赎回」在最终到期前偿还了发行债券的一部分。

examples.en: Our worksheet showed a sinking fund redemption amount in two of the years before maturity.
examples.zh: 练习表在到期前的两个年份列出了「偿债基金分期赎回」的金额。

words.zhGloss: 带补偿机制的提前赎回
words.enDefinition: an issuer's early redemption priced by a formula that discounts remaining scheduled principal and interest, subject to the terms
acceptedZhAnswers: 带补偿机制的提前赎回

examples.en: The tutor used a make-whole call to show how remaining principal and interest affect redemption pricing.
examples.zh: 导师用「带补偿机制的提前赎回」说明剩余本金和利息会怎样影响赎回定价。

examples.en: The sample indenture defined which benchmark rate applied when calculating the price of a make-whole call.
examples.zh: 样本契约规定了计算「带补偿机制的提前赎回」的价格时适用哪个基准利率。

words.enDefinition: redemption required by the bond terms when scheduled or when certain conditions are met

examples.en: The sample issue required mandatory redemption of some bonds on the dates in the schedule.
examples.zh: 示例发行要求在表列日期对部分债券进行「强制赎回」。

examples.en: We read the mandatory redemption section before calculating which notes would remain outstanding next year.
examples.zh: 我们阅读了「强制赎回」一节，再计算明年还有哪些票据未偿还。

words.enDefinition: a formal notice stating that some or all of a bond issue will be redeemed

examples.en: The fictional issuer's notice of redemption gave holders the amount and date of the upcoming payment.
examples.zh: 虚构发行人的「债券赎回通知」告诉持有人即将支付的金额和日期。

examples.en: Our class checked whether the notice of redemption covered the whole issue or only part.
examples.zh: 我们班核对了「债券赎回通知」是覆盖整个发行批次，还是只覆盖其中一部分。

words.enDefinition: a bond that repays principal in installments over its life rather than all at maturity

examples.en: The amortizing bond reduced its outstanding principal with each scheduled payment in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中的「分期偿还本金债券」每笔预定付款后都会减少未偿本金。

examples.en: Our tutor compared an amortizing bond with one that repaid principal on the final date.
examples.zh: 导师把「分期偿还本金债券」和在最后一天才偿还本金的债券作了比较。

words.enDefinition: the annualised return implied by a bond's price and payments if it is called on a specified date

examples.en: We calculated yield to call using the first eligible call date in the sample bond's terms.
examples.zh: 我们采用样本债券条款里的首次可赎回日期，计算了「赎回收益率」。

examples.en: The yield to call shown in the table assumed the issuer redeemed the note early.
examples.zh: 表中的「赎回收益率」假设发行人提前赎回票据。

collocations: compare yield to call with yield to maturity
yield to call at the first call date

words.enDefinition: the lowest of the yield to maturity and the yields for issuer call scenarios included in the calculation, assuming promised payments are made

examples.en: The table listed yield to worst beside the yields calculated for maturity and the call dates.
examples.zh: 表里把「最不利情形收益率」和按到期日、各可赎回日期计算的收益率并排列出。

examples.en: Our tutor explained why the yield to worst was lower than the yield to maturity.
examples.zh: 导师解释了为什么「最不利情形收益率」低于该债券的到期收益率。

collocations: compare yield to worst across bonds

words.enDefinition: a bond's annual coupon amount divided by its current clean market price

examples.en: We calculated current yield before considering the effect of the final repayment on total return.
examples.zh: 我们先算了「当期收益率」，再考虑最终还本对总回报的影响。

examples.en: The worksheet showed a higher current yield after we lowered the bond's example market price.
examples.zh: 调低示例债券市场价格后，练习表显示的「当期收益率」更高了。

words.enDefinition: a yield adjusted for inflation or quoted in terms of purchasing power

examples.en: The chart compared real yield with a yield before adjustment for changes in the general price level.
examples.zh: 图表比较了「实际收益率」与未经总体物价变化调整的收益率。

examples.en: The tutor explained how an inflation-linked security could be quoted using a real yield figure.
examples.zh: 导师解释了通胀挂钩证券怎样用「实际收益率」报价。

words.enDefinition: in an inflation comparison, the yield expressed before adjusting for changes in purchasing power

examples.en: We compared the nominal yield with an inflation-adjusted figure in the example for the same period.
examples.zh: 我们比较了同一时期示例中的「名义收益率」与经通胀调整的数字。

examples.en: The class checked whether the difference between nominal yield and real yield reflected the inflation assumption.
examples.zh: 我们班检查了「名义收益率」与实际收益率的差异是否反映了通胀假设。

words.enDefinition: the inflation rate implied by comparing nominal and inflation-linked bond yields at similar maturities

examples.en: We estimated the break-even inflation rate from two government securities with matching maturities in the exercise.
examples.zh: 练习中我们用两只期限匹配的政府债券估算「盈亏平衡通胀率」。

examples.en: The tutor noted that the break-even inflation rate could reflect factors besides expected changes in prices.
examples.zh: 导师指出，「盈亏平衡通胀率」还可能受到物价预期变化以外的因素影响。

words.enDefinition: an increase in the difference between longer- and shorter-term yields over the segment being compared

examples.en: The chart illustrated yield curve steepening after longer yields rose while shorter yields barely changed.
examples.zh: 长端收益率上升、短端几乎没变化，图表展示了「收益率曲线变陡」。

examples.en: We checked which maturities the analyst used to describe yield curve steepening in the example.
examples.zh: 我们查看了分析人员用哪些期限来描述示例中的「收益率曲线变陡」。

collocations: yield curve steepening at the long end

words.enDefinition: a decrease in the difference between longer- and shorter-term yields over the segment being compared

examples.en: The worksheet illustrated yield curve flattening when the shorter yield rose closer to the longer yield.
examples.zh: 短端收益率上升、向长端靠拢时，练习表展示了「收益率曲线趋平」。

examples.en: The lecturer asked what yield curve flattening meant for the gap between the two selected maturities.
examples.zh: 讲师问，「收益率曲线趋平」对所选两个期限的收益率差距意味着什么。

words.enDefinition: a measure approximating a bond's percentage price change for a small change in its own yield, assuming fixed cash flows

examples.en: Our class used modified duration to estimate how the fixed-rate bond's price would respond to higher yields.
examples.zh: 课堂上，我们用「修正久期」估算收益率升高时固定利率债券的价格如何变化。

examples.en: The analyst compared modified duration across two bonds whose cash flows were fixed in the example.
examples.zh: 在示例中，分析人员比较了两只现金流固定的债券的「修正久期」。

collocations: estimate price change using modified duration

words.enDefinition: the weighted average time to receive a bond's cash flows, weighted by their present values

examples.en: We calculated Macaulay duration using each payment's timing and its share of the total present value.
examples.zh: 我们根据每笔付款的时间和它在总现值中所占比重，计算「麦考利久期」。

examples.en: The tutor expressed Macaulay duration in years when we compared the two example bonds in class.
examples.zh: 课堂比较两只示例债券时，导师以年为单位表示「麦考利久期」。

words.enDefinition: a model-based estimate of price sensitivity to a shift in a benchmark yield curve, allowing projected cash flows to change

examples.en: The class used effective duration because the callable bond's future payments could change with interest rates.
examples.zh: 由于这只可赎回债券的未来付款可能随利率而变，课堂上用的是「有效久期」。

examples.en: The tutor compared effective duration estimates under two assumptions about whether the issuer might call the bond.
examples.zh: 导师比较了发行人是否可能赎回债券的两种假设下，「有效久期」的估算值。

collocations: effective duration of a callable bond

words.enDefinition: curvature in the relationship between bond price and yield, affecting the accuracy of a duration-only estimate

examples.en: We added a bond convexity term to improve the price estimate for the larger yield change.
examples.zh: 针对较大的收益率变化，我们加了一项「债券凸性」因素来改进价格估计。

examples.en: Our tutor used the curve to show why bond convexity mattered more for substantial yield changes.
examples.zh: 导师用这条曲线说明，为什么收益率变化较大时「债券凸性」更重要。

words.enDefinition: the possibility that cash received from an investment will have to be reinvested at a lower return

examples.en: The case illustrated reinvestment risk when coupons received early could earn less than the original bond.
examples.zh: 案例展示了「再投资风险」：提前收到的票息再投资后，回报可能低于原债券。

examples.en: We discussed reinvestment risk after the example issuer called the bond during a period of falling rates.
examples.zh: 示例发行人在利率下降时赎回债券后，我们讨论了「再投资风险」。

words.enDefinition: a US Treasury security used as a reference when quoting or comparing another bond's yield

examples.en: The offering sheet named a benchmark Treasury used to calculate the spread on the new bond.
examples.zh: 发行说明指定了一只「作为基准的美国国债」，用于计算新债的利差。

examples.en: We compared the yield on the benchmark Treasury with the new bond's yield in class.
examples.zh: 我们在课上对比了「作为基准的美国国债」和这只新债券的收益率。

words.enDefinition: in a Treasury auction, a bid specifying the yield, discount rate or discount margin sought

examples.en: The example showed a competitive bid alongside the final yield reported for that Treasury auction.
examples.zh: 示例把「竞争性投标」与本次国债拍卖通报的最终收益率并排列出。

examples.en: Our tutor explained why a competitive bid could be accepted in full or only in part.
examples.zh: 导师解释了为什么「竞争性投标」可能被全额接受，也可能只中标一部分。

collocations: competitive bid at a Treasury auction

words.enDefinition: in a Treasury auction, a bid accepting the rate, yield or discount margin determined at auction

examples.en: The worksheet showed how a noncompetitive bid used the auction result without specifying a requested yield.
examples.zh: 练习表展示了「非竞争性投标」如何采用拍卖结果，无须事先指定所要求的收益率。

examples.en: The tutor used a noncompetitive bid to explain one of the award categories in the results.
examples.zh: 导师用「非竞争性投标」说明拍卖结果中的一种获配类别。

collocations: noncompetitive bid at a Treasury auction

words.enDefinition: the ratio of the amount bid for in a debt auction to the amount awarded, under the auction's definitions

examples.en: The bid-to-cover ratio rose as the amount bid increased and the amount awarded stayed roughly the same.
examples.zh: 投标额增加而获配额大致保持稳定，「投标额与获配额之比」随之上升。

examples.en: The tutor showed where to find the bid-to-cover ratio on the sample Treasury auction result.
examples.zh: 导师指给我们看，国债拍卖结果样本里哪里能查到「投标额与获配额之比」。

words.enDefinition: an auction offering more of a security that was previously issued

examples.en: The auction reopening offered more of the same note without changing its original maturity date.
examples.zh: 「同一证券追加拍卖」提供了同一只票据的更多份额，原到期日保持原样。

examples.en: Our class compared an auction reopening with the first auction of a new Treasury security.
examples.zh: 我们班把「同一证券追加拍卖」与一只新国债的首场拍卖作了比较。

words.enDefinition: the smallest principal amount of a security that can be purchased or held under its terms

examples.en: The offering document stated the minimum denomination before listing the increments allowed above that amount.
examples.zh: 发行文件先列「最低认购面额」，再列超过该金额后的允许递增档。

examples.en: Our worksheet asked whether the example amount met the minimum denomination of the issued note.
examples.zh: 练习表问，示例金额是否达到所发票据的「最低认购面额」。

words.zhGloss: 最低面额以上的递增单位
words.enDefinition: the size of additional principal increments permitted above the minimum denomination in an offering
acceptedZhAnswers: 最低面额以上的递增单位

examples.en: The terms listed an incremental denomination that applied after the initial minimum amount was met.
examples.zh: 条款规定，达到初始最低金额后，要按「最低面额以上的递增单位」增加。

examples.en: The adviser pointed to the incremental denomination to explain which amounts were permitted in the example.
examples.zh: 顾问指出「最低面额以上的递增单位」，以解释示例中允许哪些金额。
